The Wednesday catalysts are concrete and mutually reinforcing across all three tier surfaces simultaneously: SGLang RadixArk v0.5.7 and Hugging Face TGI v3.2.0 ship the signed-checkpoint loader as the documented default load path for new installs on the same Wednesday (becoming the second and third open-source serving stacks at the serving tier inside one week, with SGLang the first to default it); Unsloth ships the workflow-state path-canonicalization mitigation in its Wednesday changelog tied to the AutoGen CVE-2026-44918 disclosure and the v2 joint preprint, becoming the first local-LLM fine-tuning stack to ship the workflow-state mitigation alongside the signed-checkpoint primitive ahead of the framework cohort's coordinated mid-June default-shipment target now extended to cover all three tier surfaces; the DeepMind plus Meta AI plus Anthropic plus Microsoft Wednesday v2 joint preprint addendum extends the Tuesday runtime-verifier integration to the workflow-state tier with reference implementations in Python and Rust; the Yotta Labs canonical benchmark refresh holds the vLLM-SGLang RadixArk throughput gap at 9.1 percent (essentially flat from Tuesday's 9.4 percent) with both stacks gaining 3 to 4 percent absolute throughput; the Cloudflare Infire L40S advantage closes to 1.12x (vs 1.18x Tuesday) with parity projected at vLLM v0.11.4 on Monday May 18; and Stable Long-Context RL via Router-Aware Advantage Decomposition v6 (arxiv 2605.05844 v6) demonstrates pre-tested integration against all three serving-stack loaders simultaneously — the first three-stack training-and-serving end-to-end formal-verification chain at the local-LLM workstation tier. The structural force is that once two production-tier serving stacks default the signed-checkpoint loader on the same Wednesday a leading local-LLM fine-tuning stack ships the workflow-state mitigation, and the v2 runtime-verifier preprint plus the Wednesday Verifiable Workflow-State Path Canonicalization paper (arxiv 2605.06799) anchor the cohort with reference implementations in Python and Rust covering all nine CVE-pattern instances, the remaining workstation-tier maintainers cannot leave unsigned or unmitigated loading as the documented default while the cyber-eval reciprocity attestation field schema and the CISA federal-civilian operational-directive working draft treat signed-load posture as paired procurement-eligibility evidence. The most likely shape is the three-tier mitigation becoming the default load path in the next minor release of llama.cpp, MLX, Ollama, and Foundry Local by Q3 2026 with explicit unsigned-load opt-out flags for sandboxed test fixtures and reproduction harnesses; sovereign-cloud and on-prem FedRAMP-Moderate workstation deployments adopt the loader first because the twelve-jurisdiction Indo-Pacific cohort exposes signed-load posture as a tenant-policy field. Bear case is that one workstation-tier stack ships a sandbox-only mitigation or forks the loader contract; absent that, Q3 2026 lands three-tier signed-load mitigation as the documented default at the local-LLM workstation tier across the eight-stack cohort.
linked_predictions.prediction_short_label: Local-LLM workstations ship three-tier signed-load default by Q3 2026

linked_predictions.prediction_summary: By Q4 2026 the Tuesday serving-tier and local-LLM-stack adoption of the DeepMind plus Meta AI plus Anthropic plus Microsoft joint signed-checkpoint reference implementation forces the open-source inference-serving cohort — vLLM, SGLang, TGI, TensorRT-LLM, Triton Inference Server, and Ray Serve — to ship signature-verified model-checkpoint loading as the documented default load path at the serving tier rather than as an opt-in feature. The Tuesday catalysts are concrete and mutually reinforcing: vLLM v0.11.3 ships a Tuesday point release adding a Sigstore-or-cosign-compatible signature-verified model-checkpoint loader and becomes the first open-source serving stack to ship the signed-checkpoint primitive at the serving tier; Unsloth ships the same primitive at the local-LLM fine-tuning stack tier on the same day, the first local-LLM stack to do so ahead of the framework cohort's coordinated mid-June default-shipment target; the Cloudflare Infire production-deployment note reports the new loader plus the tensor-parallel disaggregated-prefill mode close the L40S edge-tier latency gap to a 1.18x Infire advantage (down from 1.25x at the v0.11.2 Monday checkpoint) with a parity-window targeted at v0.11.4 in late-May; the Yotta Labs canonical benchmark refresh places vLLM v0.11.3 at approximately 16,580 tok/s on the shared-prefix workload versus 18,140 tok/s on SGLang RadixArk v0.5.6, narrowing the throughput gap to 9.4 percent from 11.3 percent Monday; and the Tuesday DeepMind plus Meta AI plus Anthropic plus Microsoft joint follow-up preprint (arxiv 2605.06712) extends the Monday signed-checkpoint format to cover the inference-routing tier and explicitly anchors the runtime-verifier integration pattern to vLLM, SGLang, TGI, and TensorRT-LLM as the reference serving stacks. The structural force is that once one production-tier serving stack ships signature-verified loading on the same day a leading local-LLM fine-tuning stack ships the matching primitive, and the runtime-verifier preprint anchors the cohort with named reference implementations, the remaining serving-tier maintainers cannot leave unsigned checkpoint loading as the documented default while the cyber-eval reciprocity attestation field schema and the CISA KEV cadence treat signed-load posture as paired procurement-eligibility evidence; the convergence of the vLLM-SGLang throughput gap to single digits removes the last performance argument for postponing the change. The most likely shape is the signed-checkpoint loader becoming the default load path in the next minor release of SGLang RadixArk, TGI, TensorRT-LLM, Triton Inference Server, and Ray Serve, with an explicit unsigned-load opt-out flag for sandboxed test fixtures and reproduction harnesses; sovereign-cloud and FedRAMP-Moderate serving tenants adopt the loader first because the Indo-Pacific eleven-jurisdiction cohort plus the AWS Bedrock and Google Cloud Vertex agent-registry public-preview interop already exposes signed-load posture as a tenant-policy field. Bear case is that one serving stack forks the loader contract or ships a sandbox-only mitigation; absent that, Q4 2026 lands signature-verified model-checkpoint loading as the documented default at the serving tier across the open-source cohort.
linked_predictions.prediction_short_label: Open-source serving stacks ship signed-checkpoint loading as default by Q4 2026

linked_predictions.prediction_summary: By Q4 2026 the May 9 disaggregated-prefill convergence forces prefill/decode disaggregation out of the Cloudflare-Infire-specific edge architecture and into the documented default serving mode shipped by vLLM and SGLang at the H100 and L40S tiers. The catalysts landing across a single weekend cycle are concrete and mutually reinforcing: vLLM v0.11.1 ships a disaggregated-prefill mode that, per Cloudflare Infire engineering's Saturday benchmark note, reaches parity with the production Infire edge architecture on prefill throughput at the H100 tier, with Infire retaining only a 1.4x advantage at the L40S edge tier on decode-side latency rather than the order-of-magnitude gap that previously kept disaggregation out of the open-source serving stack; the Yotta Labs benchmark refresh holds the canonical shared-prefix workload at approximately 14,650 tok/s on vLLM versus 17,300 tok/s on SGLang RadixArk, narrowing the throughput gap to a level where the architectural choice (monolithic vs disaggregated) dominates the remaining delta; SGLang RadixArk v0.5.4 ships a parallel architectural primitive in the form of RadixAttention-aware tool-result-cache reuse delivering a 2.1x speedup on tool-calling-heavy agentic workloads, demonstrating that the radix-tree cache substrate generalizes from prefix sharing to tool-call result sharing; and Trail of Bits's full red-team write-up on SGLang RadixArk CVE-2026-44567 (CVSS 8.1 authenticated server-side template injection) plus the v0.11.1 patch for the prefix-cache poisoning CVE-2026-44512 disclosed Friday convert the security narrative from a blocker to a documented disclosure-timeline pattern. The structural force is that once Cloudflare Infire engineering publishes a benchmark showing parity at the H100 tier between its production edge architecture and an open-source serving stack's disaggregated mode, downstream framework maintainers can cite the production-comparable benchmark rather than ship monolithic-mode defaults, and the SGLang radix-tree cache substrate gives a parallel architectural lineage that converges on the same shape. The most likely shape is a disaggregated-prefill/decode mode added as the documented default in the vLLM v0.12 and SGLang RadixArk v0.6 release lines, with per-tier deployment templates targeting H100 single-node and L40S edge-tier topology, plus a Yotta-style canonical benchmark harness gating the production-readiness claim. Sovereign-cloud and on-prem agentic-AI workloads adopt it first because the tool-result-cache reuse substrate compounds the latency win for long tool-call chains. Bear case is a competing serving-stack architecture refusing the disaggregation split and forking the benchmark methodology; absent that, Q4 2026 lands disaggregated prefill as the documented default across the open-source serving cohort.
linked_predictions.prediction_short_label: Disaggregated prefill ships as vLLM and SGLang serving default by Q4 2026

linked_predictions.prediction_summary: By Q4 2026 the May 8 router-only LoRA convergence — the Unsloth + Hugging Face joint arxiv preprint reporting 71-78% recovery of full-LoRA-on-experts accuracy at 8-13% of training-step time and 11-16% of peak VRAM across a four-model ablation (Qwen3.6-Max, Mixtral 8x22B, DBRX, Kimi K2.6), Unsloth's same-day production recipes for Llama 4 Behemoth single-node tuning, Kimi K2.6 on a 96GB workstation, and Mixtral 8x22B for sovereign-cloud customers, the parallel DeepMind preprint on router-aware advantage decomposition closing the long-context Reinforcement Learning stability gap that previously kept router-only mode out of ultra-long-context training, and Cerebras's CS-4 engineering-sample announcement explicitly naming Mixture-of-Experts router-only training plus ultra-long-context Reinforcement Learning as the target workload — together force the router-only adaptation mode out of the Unsloth-specific category and into the default fine-tuning recipe shipped by every major training stack inside the same calendar window. The structural force is that the four-model ablation gives downstream framework maintainers a published parity baseline they can target without re-running the search, and the DeepMind stability proof removes the last operational reason to keep training all expert weights for a router-shaped objective. The most likely shape is a router-only adapter type added as a first-class option in Hugging Face PEFT, NVIDIA NeMo, Microsoft DeepSpeed, and Meta's torchtune, with default recipe templates targeting at least the Llama, Qwen, and Mixtral families; sovereign-cloud customers and on-prem RTX 6000 Ada workstation tier buyers adopt it first because the VRAM reduction is the only path to single-node tuning of Behemoth-class MoE models. Bear case is a competing scaling-law preprint showing the accuracy gap widens past 200B parameters and forcing a hybrid mode; absent that, Q4 2026 lands router-only as the documented default across the cohort.
